'''Nikola Peković''' ([[Serbian Cyrillic script|Serbian Cyrillic]]: Никола Пековић; born 3 January 1986) is a Montenegrin businessman, [[basketball]] executive and former professional player who is the current president of the [[Basketball Federation of Montenegro]]. He began his playing career in Europe before spending seven years with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=11}}, he played at the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. A two-time [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague selection]], he represented the senior [[Montenegro national basketball team|Montenegrin national basketball team]].

==Professional career==

===Early years===
Peković began playing basketball with a junior team from [[Podgorica]] at the age of 15.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://sport.blic.rs/Kosarka/90486/Pokoriti-Evropu | title=Pokoriti Evropu | language=sr | publisher=Blic.rs | date=30 April 2009 | access-date=20 February 2013}}</ref> In 2003, he moved to [[Belgrade]], [[Serbia]] and signed his first professional contract with [[KK Atlas|Atlas]] during the summer.

===Partizan (2005–2008)===
After two years there, Peković joined the national champions Partizan in July 2005. With Black and Whites, he won three consecutive Basketball League of Serbia titles, two Adriatic League and Radivoj Korać Cup titles. Peković was named the MVP of the Adriatic League Final Four in 2008. The same year, he also earned an All-Euroleague Second Team selection for leading Partizan to the competition's quarterfinals.

===Panathinaikos (2008–2010)===
In the summer of 2008, Peković joined the Greek champions [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/33029/180 | title=Panathinaikos inks Pekovic, brings back Fotsis | publisher=Euroleague.net | date=24 June 2008 | access-date=20 February 2013}}</ref> He signed a three-year contract worth [[Euro sign|€]]4.5 million [[net income]]. He averaged 13.0 points and 3.8 rebounds in just over 18 minutes per contest, helping Panathinaikos win the [[2008–09 Euroleague|2008–09 EuroLeague]] title. Peković consequently established himself as one of Europe's elite centers, being voted to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/49917/2768 | title=Tribute to the champs, Panathinaikos: Nikola Pekovic! | publisher=Euroleague.net | date=22 May 2009 | access-date=20 February 2013}}</ref> With PAO, he also won two [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] titles and the 2009 [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]].

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2010–2017)===
[[File:20140101 Nikola Peković guarded by Anthony Davis (1).JPG|thumb|right|Peković guarded by [[Anthony Davis]] in 2014|200px]]
Peković was selected with the 31st overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Many draft experts considered him a top 10 pick, but due to his contract situation with his team in Europe, he was selected much lower. He was considered a lock to be drafted with the first pick of the second round because players selected in the second round are not subject to the rookie scale contracts of the first round. This meant that the team that drafted him would be able to pay him more than those players selected later in the first round. Due to the amount of money Peković was making in Europe already, he likely would not have made the jump to the NBA for the amount of money that could be paid to a late first round player.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

====Rookie season (2010–2011)====
On 30 June 2010, two years after being drafted, Peković signed a three-year, $13 million contract with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5344931 | title=Sources: Pekovic's deal worth $13M | work=ESPN.com | date=30 June 2010 | access-date=20 February 2013}}</ref> As a rookie in the NBA in 2010–11, Peković averaged 5.5 points and 3.0 rebounds per game.

On 16 August 2011, Peković signed a contract to play for his former team Partizan until the end of the [[2011 NBA lockout]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/87174/partizan-brings-former-all-euroleaguer-pekovic-home | title=Partizan brings former All-Euroleaguer Pekovic home | work=Euroleague.net | date=16 August 2011 | access-date=20 February 2013}}</ref> In 7 Euroleague games with Partizan, he led the team averaging 15.4 points and 4.6 rebounds. As the NBA lockout ended on 8 December 2011, he had to return to the United States.

====Rise to prominence (2011–2014)====
The 2011–12 shortened NBA season started on 25 December 2011. Upon returning to Minnesota, through January 2012, Peković stepped in for an injured [[Darko Miličić]] as the starting center for the Timberwolves. He finished the 2011–12 season with 13.9 points and 7.4 rebounds in 26.9 minutes per game. In voting for the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player]], Peković finished third behind Orlando's [[Ryan Anderson (basketball, born 1988)|Ryan Anderson]] and Milwaukee's [[Ersan İlyasova]].

During the 2012–13 NBA season, Peković cemented his position of starting center and with team's superstar [[Kevin Love]], led the Timberwolves frontcourt. With 31–51 record, it was the first season since [[Kevin Garnett]]'s departure that the Timberwolves won more than 30 regular season games. Peković averaged 16.3 points and career-high 8.8 rebounds per game.

On 14 August 2013, Peković re-signed with the Timberwolves to a five-year, $60 million deal.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-reach-agreement-principle-restricted-free-agent-center-nikola-pekovic | title=Timberwolves Reach Agreement in Principle with Restricted Free-Agent Center Nikola Pekovic | work=NBA.com | date=14 August 2013 | access-date=14 August 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | last=Zgoda | first=Jerry | url=http://www.startribune.com/wolves-center-nikola-pekovic-agrees-to-5-year-60m-contract/219605101/ | title=It's done: Pek agrees to 5-year, $60M deal | work=StarTribune.com | date=14 August 2013 | access-date=14 August 2013}}</ref> On 27 January 2014, he suffered an ankle injury that hindered him for the rest of the season; he played only 10 games until the end of the season. The 2013–14 season for the Timberwolves was even more successful than previous as they managed to win 40 games. Over the season, Peković averaged a career-high 17.5 points and 8.7 rebounds over 54 regular season games.

In August 2014, the Timberwolves traded Love in a three-team trade receiving [[Andrew Wiggins]], starting the new era of the franchise.

====Injury-plagued seasons (2014–2017)====
During the 2014–15 season, Peković managed to play only 31 games due to a right ankle injury, averaging 12.5 points per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/roster-review-nikola-pekovic |title=Roster Review - Nikola Pekovic|work=Minnesota Timberwolves|publisher=NBA}}</ref> On 8 April 2015, Peković had surgery on his right Achilles tendon in hopes of addressing the pain in his bothersome right foot.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/12649475/minnesota-timberwolves-center-nikola-pekovic-undergoes-surgery-right-achilles-tendon|title=Minnesota Timberwolves center Nikola Pekovic undergoes surgery on right Achilles tendon|date=8 April 2015|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> The departure of Love, Peković's absence from the court and other factors resulted in the worst league record of 16–66 for the Timberwolves. Eventually the Timberwolves won the [[NBA draft lottery|draft lottery]] and selected [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] with the first overall pick, strengthening their core of young talented players in Wiggins and [[Zach LaVine]].

Entering his third season of a new contract, Peković was still enduring chronically sore ankles and Achilles. He made his season debut for the Timberwolves on 6 January 2016, playing for the first time since 11 March 2015. In 16 minutes of action off the bench, he scored 12 points in a loss to the Denver Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160106/DENMIN/gameinfo.html|title=Gallinari, Nuggets snap 6-game skid with win over Wolves|date=6 January 2016|work=Game Story|publisher=NBA|access-date=7 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160108034835/http://www.nba.com/games/20160106/DENMIN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=8 January 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Over the season, he appeared in just 12 games, averaging career lows of 4.5 points and 1.8 rebounds.

On 25 September 2016, Peković was ruled out for the entire 2016–17 season due to recurring right ankle pain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/nikola-pekovic-injury-update-9-25-2016|title=NIKOLA PEKOVIC INJURY UPDATE|work=NBA.com|date=25 September 2016|access-date=25 September 2016}}</ref> At the time, it appeared unlikely Peković would ever return to the court with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hellin|first1=Kurt|title=Tom Thibodeau doesn't expect Nikola Pekovic to play in training camp|url=http://nba.nbcsports.com/2016/09/21/tom-thibodeau-doesnt-expect-nikola-pekovic-to-play-in-training-camp/|access-date=21 September 2016|work=nbcsports.com|date=21 September 2016}}</ref> On 20 June 2017, following the conclusion of the 2016–17 season, Peković was waived by the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-waive-center-nikola-pekovic|title=TIMBERWOLVES WAIVE CENTER NIKOLA PEKOVIC|work=NBA.com|date=20 June 2017|access-date=20 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Maloney|first1=Jack|title=Minnesota Timberwolves waive oft-injured big man Nikola Pekovic|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/timberwolves-waive-oft-injured-big-man-nikola-pekovic/|access-date=20 June 2017|work=cbssports.com|date=20 June 2017}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Nikola Pekovic.jpg|thumb|right|Peković with Montenegro in 2010|200px]]

===Serbia and Montenegro junior national team===
While playing with the youth national teams of Serbia and Montenegro, Peković received the bronze medal at the [[2005 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2005]] [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|European Under-20 Championship]], in [[Russia]]. He also won the gold medal with his generation at the [[2006 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2006 tournament]], which was held in [[Turkey]].

===Montenegro national team===
Peković represented the senior [[Montenegro national basketball team|Montenegrin national team]] at the [[EuroBasket 2011]], which was held in Lithuania. Over 5 tournament games, he averaged 13.0 points and 6.4 rebounds per game, as Montenegro finished the tournament after being eliminated after the first phase.

==Executive career==
===KK Partizan===
In September 2015, Peković accepted an offer by the [[KK Partizan]] board of directors of becoming the club's new president, following the late August 2015 resignation of [[Predrag Danilović|Sasha Danilović]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Peković od utorka na čelu Partizana|url=http://mondo.rs/a827828/Sport/Kosarka/KK-Partizan-Nikola-Pekovic-novi-predsednik-zakazana-vanredna-Skupstina.html|access-date=6 October 2015|work=mondo.rs|date=7 September 2015|language=sr}}</ref> Soon after taking the position, he hired [[Petar Božić]] to be the club's new [[head coach]], thus not offering [[Duško Vujošević]] a new contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Božić novi trener Partizana!|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2015&mm=09&dd=08&nav_id=1036628|access-date=6 October 2015|work=b92.net|date=8 September 2015|language=sr}}</ref>

On 14 June 2017, he resigned from the position.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nikola Peković podneo ostavku!|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2017&mm=06&dd=14&nav_id=1271951|access-date=14 June 2017|work=b92.net|date=14 June 2017|language=sr}}</ref>

===Montenegrin Basketball Federation (KSCG)===
In January 2020, Peković became a team manager for the [[Montenegro national basketball team]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Peković tim menadžer reprezentacije Crne Gore |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2020&mm=01&dd=10&nav_id=1640202 |website=b92.net |access-date=10 January 2020}}</ref> while on 26 April 2020 he was named the president of the [[Basketball Federation of Montenegro]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nikola Peković novi predsjednik Košarkaškog saveza Crne Gore|url=https://www.vijesti.me/sport/kosarka/533673/nikola-pekovic-novi-predsjednik-kosarkaskog-saveza-crne-gore|access-date=26 April 2021|website=vijesti.me|language=sr}}</ref> Few hours prior to being named on this position, Peković met with [[Deputy Prime Minister of Montenegro|Deputy Prime Minister]] [[Dritan Abazović]], with the two holding a meeting about the future of basketball in Montenegro.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Abazović sa Pekovićem i Radovićem o košarkaškim temama|url=https://www.vijesti.me/sport/kosarka/533637/abazovic-sa-pekovicem-i-radovicem-o-kosarkaskim-temama|access-date=26 April 2021|website=vijesti.me|language=sr}}</ref>

In June 2022, [[KK Zlatibor|Zlatibor]] added Peković as a member of their managing board.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ponovo u srpskoj košarci: Nikola Peković sa Zlatiborom cilja ABA ligu! |url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/ponovo-u-srpskoj-kosarci-nikola-pekovic-sa-zlatiborom-cilja-aba-ligu/423314 |website=mozzartsport.com |access-date=22 June 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Peković is an ethnic [[Serbs of Montenegro|Serb]] and a [[Serbian Orthodox Church|Serbian Orthodox Christian]].<ref name="Kurir">{{cite web|url=http://www.kurir.rs/sa-tri-prsta-nikola-pekovic-nagovorio-igrace-minesote-da-se-slikaju-kao-srbi-clanak-1174165|title=SA TRI PRSTA: Nikola Peković nagovorio igrače Minesote da se slikaju kao Srbi|work=Kurir sport|date=16 October 2023 |publisher=Kurir}}</ref> He spends his off-seasons in Serbia, particularly in [[Zlatibor]] where he has built an apartment house, as well as in [[Belgrade]].<ref name="Hello">{{cite web|url=http://www.hellomagazin.rs/intervju/nikola-pekovic-prizeljkujem-da-se-skrasim-ali-sam-dosta-komplikovan/|title=Nikola Peković: Priželjkujem da se skrasim, ali sam dosta komplikovan|work=Intervju|publisher=Hello! magazin}}</ref> He has several Serb-themed tattoos, including the [[Battle of Kosovo]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html:461356-Pekovic-istetovirao-Boj-na-Kosovu-Amerikanci-se-cude-tetovazi-sa-motivom-bitke-koju-je-srpska-vojska-izgubila|title=Peković istetovirao Boj na Kosovu, Amerikanci se čude tetovaži sa motivom bitke koju je srpska vojska izgubila|work=Sport|publisher=Novosti}}</ref> and the [[Serbian cross]].<ref name="Kurir"/>

Peković is connected to several underworld figures, most notably Montenegrin drug lord [[Darko Šarić]] who has been held in custody since 2011.<ref name="saric">{{cite news|last1=Jovićević|first1=Mihailo|title=PEKOVIĆEV BIZNIS U SENCI ŠARIĆEVOG KLANA Poznati košarkaš ulaže MILIONE u sumnjive poslove, a pomaže mu KUM|url=http://www.blic.rs/vesti/hronika/pekovicev-biznis-u-senci-saricevog-klana-poznati-kosarkas-ulaze-milione-u-sumnjive/47ntcvd|access-date=29 November 2017|work=blic.rs|date=28 November 2017|language=sr}}</ref> Peković has numerous business investments with Šarić in Serbia and Montenegro.<ref name="saric" /> In October 2018, Peković took over a 1.15-million-euro debt from Šarić's brother.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nikola Peković preuzeo milionske dugove brata Darka Šarića |url=https://www.b92.net/info/vesti/index.php?yyyy=2018&mm=10&dd=31&nav_category=16&nav_id=1463543 |access-date=31 October 2018 |work=b92.net |date=31 October 2018 |language=sr}}</ref>

On 10 October 2020, Peković was reported to have been hospitalized after being infected by [[Coronavirus disease 2019|coronavirus]].<ref>{{cite web|first1=Antonis|last1=Stroggylakis|title=Nikola Pekovic hospitalized with coronavirus|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/backstage/1112301/nikola-pekovic-reportedly-hospitalized-in-serious-condition-with-coronavirus|date=10 October 2020|website=eurohoops.net|access-date=10 October 2020}}</ref>
